blocks.prompt: 7 If \(a^{2}, b^{2}\) and \(c^{2}\) are in A.P., show that \(a + b\), \(c + a\) and \(b + c\) are in H.P.
blocks.explanation:
A proof. To show three numbers are in H.P. we show their reciprocals are in A.P.
So we must show \(\frac{1}{a + b}, \frac{1}{c + a}, \frac{1}{b + c}\) have equal differences.
Plan: compute both differences and use the given \(b^{2} - a^{2} = c^{2} - b^{2}\).
steps:
Given: \(a^{2}, b^{2}, c^{2}\) are in A.P., so
\[b^{2} - a^{2} = c^{2} - b^{2}\]
To prove: \(a + b, c + a, b + c\) are in H.P. (sums assumed non-zero).
Method: Show \(\frac{1}{c + a} - \frac{1}{a + b} = \frac{1}{b + c} - \frac{1}{c + a}\).

First difference of reciprocals
\[\dfrac{1}{c + a} - \dfrac{1}{a + b}\]
\[= \dfrac{(a + b) - (c + a)}{(c + a)(a + b)}\]
\[= \dfrac{b - c}{(c + a)(a + b)}\]
Why: Common denominator; \(a\) cancels on top.

Second difference of reciprocals
\[\dfrac{1}{b + c} - \dfrac{1}{c + a}\]
\[= \dfrac{(c + a) - (b + c)}{(b + c)(c + a)}\]
\[= \dfrac{a - b}{(b + c)(c + a)}\]
Why: Same method; \(c\) cancels on top.

Turn each into a difference of squares
Let \(D = (a + b)(b + c)(c + a)\).
\[\dfrac{b - c}{(c + a)(a + b)} = \dfrac{(b - c)(b + c)}{D}\]
\[= \dfrac{b^{2} - c^{2}}{D}\]
\[\dfrac{a - b}{(b + c)(c + a)} = \dfrac{(a - b)(a + b)}{D}\]
\[= \dfrac{a^{2} - b^{2}}{D}\]
Why: Multiplying top and bottom by the missing factor gives both fractions the same denominator.

Use the given condition
\[b^{2} - a^{2} = c^{2} - b^{2}\]
\[\Rightarrow b^{2} - c^{2} = a^{2} - b^{2}\]
Why: Multiply both sides by \(-1\) and swap sides. So the two tops are equal, and the denominators are equal.

Conclude
\[\dfrac{1}{c + a} - \dfrac{1}{a + b} = \dfrac{1}{b + c} - \dfrac{1}{c + a}\]
Why: Equal differences mean \(\frac{1}{a + b}, \frac{1}{c + a}, \frac{1}{b + c}\) are in A.P., hence \(a + b, c + a, b + c\) are in H.P.

Check with numbers: \(a = 1, b = 5, c = 7\) give \(1, 25, 49\) (A.P., \(d = 24\)). Then \(a + b = 6\), \(c + a = 8\), \(b + c = 12\); reciprocals \(\frac{1}{6}, \frac{1}{8}, \frac{1}{12}\) have difference \(-\frac{1}{24}\) each \(\checkmark\).
blocks.final_answer: Hence proved: \(a + b, \; c + a, \; b + c\) are in H.P.
